title: A Mentor Talks a Student Out of Procrastinating on Her Thesis
script: Professor Hana: [thoughtful] Wulan, you've submitted almost nothing since our last meeting. What's actually going on with the thesis?
Wulan: Honestly, I keep opening the document and closing it again without writing a single sentence.
Professor Hana: [carefully] Is the barrier scope, evidence, method, language, access, wellbeing, fear of imperfection, or something else? I will not diagnose it from one answer.
Wulan: The second one, I think. Every sentence feels wrong as soon as I type it.
Professor Hana: [reflective] That's more common than you'd expect, even among students who eventually write excellent theses.
Wulan: Really? You always seem so certain about everything you publish.
Professor Hana: [honestly] My first drafts are rough. I protect student and research confidentiality and do not share supervised work with family or unauthorized readers.
Wulan: I suppose I assumed good writers just produce good sentences immediately, without all this struggling.
Professor Hana: [seriously] That assumption is exactly what's paralyzing you. Writing badly first is not a failure, it's simply the process.
Wulan: So you're suggesting I just write something terrible on purpose?
Professor Hana: [gently] In a sense, yes. Draft one bounded paragraph with honest sources. Rough work still follows citation, research ethics, data security, originality, and permitted-tool rules.
Wulan: What if the rough version is so bad that revising feels impossible too?
Professor Hana: [encouraging] Then we revise it together, sentence by sentence, until it says roughly what you mean.
Wulan: That actually sounds manageable, unlike the vague pressure of writing a flawless chapter alone.
Professor Hana: [sincere] Exactly. Send one rough page through the official secure channel by our agreed deadline; then we can identify the next specific support.
Wulan: Okay. Even if it's messy, I'll send something rather than nothing this time.
Professor Hana: [thoughtful] Good. And Wulan, the blank page will always feel worse than any imperfect page you actually write.
Wulan: I will also stop treating midnight work as the only path and use academic-skills, disability, language, or wellbeing support if relevant.

quiz.question: What has Wulan been doing instead of writing?
options: Opening the document and closing it without writing anything
quiz.explanation: Wulan admits she keeps opening the document and closing it again without writing a single sentence.

quiz.question: What does Wulan say is really stopping her from writing?
quiz.explanation: Wulan admits she fears writing badly, since every sentence feels wrong as soon as she types it.

quiz.question: What does Professor Hana reveal about her own writing process?
options: Her first drafts are embarrassing and only she and her husband see them
She writes perfectly on the first try
quiz.explanation: Professor Hana admits her first drafts are embarrassing, seen only by her and occasionally her husband.

quiz.question: What does Professor Hana say writing badly first actually is?
quiz.explanation: She tells Wulan that writing badly first is not a failure, it's simply the process.

quiz.question: What does Professor Hana ask Wulan to send by Friday?
options: One rough page, regardless of how unfinished it feels
quiz.explanation: Professor Hana asks Wulan to send one rough page by Friday, regardless of how unfinished it feels.

quiz.question: What is Professor Hana careful not to diagnose?
options: Whether the thesis has a title
The cause of Wulan’s avoidance from a brief conversation
quiz.explanation: Similar behavior may have different causes.

quiz.question: Why is one rough page useful?
options: Bad writing should be submitted as final
It is a bounded diagnostic step that can receive specific feedback
quiz.explanation: A small artifact reveals where support is needed.

quiz.question: What rules still apply to a rough draft?
options: No academic rules apply before final submission
Private data may be pasted anywhere
Citation, research ethics, data security, originality, and disclosed permitted assistance
quiz.explanation: Draft status does not suspend integrity.

quiz.question: How are boundaries protected?
options: Feedback uses official secure channels and agreed hours rather than private family access or midnight pressure

quiz.question: What broader support may be relevant?
options: Academic-skills, disability, language, wellbeing, or research-method support according to need
